email.subject: Last chance to collect your parcel

body.v: Your parcel has been waiting at the pick-up point for 6 days. If it isn't collected, it will go back to the sender tomorrow.
Collection is free. Bring an ID document and the code shown in the ParcelPoint app.
Opening hours are shown in the app.

hotspots.explain: The address ends in parcelpoint.example, the real domain.
The deadline is real, but all you're asked to do is collect your parcel. Urgency on its own doesn't make a scam.
Collection is free. That's exactly where a scam would slip in a fee.
It sends you to the app you already have, not to a link.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: ParcelPoint: the address is on the real domain, and everything points to the app.
choices: A neighbour who kept the parcel

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: A little urgency, since the parcel goes back tomorrow. But that pressure comes from a real deadline, not a ploy.
choices: The hope of winning a contest
A little urgency, from a real deadline

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Collect your parcel in person. No payment, no sign-in, no link.

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself to see the pick-up point and your code. The email itself sends you there.
choices: Click a link in the email
Reply and ask for more time

actions.label: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and check the collection details
actions.consequence: The parcel and its collection code are both there.

actions.label: Collect the parcel from the pick-up point
actions.consequence: You show your ID and the code. Nobody asks you for money.

actions.label: Reply and offer to pay for an extension
actions.consequence: Nobody reads replies to this address. And there was nothing to pay anyway.

attacker_reveal: Yes, there's a deadline. And no, it isn't me: right domain, not a franc asked for, and it sends you to the app. A deadline alone doesn't make an alarm. Look at what they want from you.
